content.user_title: Write App Changelogs from Git History
content.value_statement: Release teams need clear changelog text without manually reading every commit. This skill reviews git history, filters user-facing changes, and updates the latest app changelog.
actual_capabilities: Fetches and reviews git tags to find the latest release baseline.
Collects commit titles and descriptions since the selected version tag.
Filters out infrastructure, CI, build, and internal documentation changes.
Selects the most important user-facing changes for the release note.
Matches the style of existing Fastlane Android changelog entries.
Updates the highest numbered changelog file with concise release text.
limitations: It depends on meaningful commit messages and accurate version tags.
It focuses on Android Fastlane changelog files in the documented path.
It may need human review for ambiguous technical changes.
It does not generate release notes for every locale automatically.

use_cases.title: Prepare Android Release Notes
use_cases.description: Create concise Store-ready changelog text from commits since the last version tag.

use_cases.title: Summarize User-Facing Changes
use_cases.description: Filter development noise and focus on features, bug fixes, and performance improvements.

use_cases.title: Keep Changelog Style Consistent
use_cases.description: Match the tone and format of previous Fastlane changelog files before updating the latest entry.

prompt_templates.title: Draft the Latest Changelog
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner request for a standard release update.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the write-app-change-log skill to review commits since the latest v* tag and update the latest Fastlane changelog file.

prompt_templates.title: Focus on User Impact
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate request when many commits are not user-facing.
prompt_templates.prompt: Generate a changelog that excludes infrastructure, CI, build tooling, and internal documentation changes. Keep only user-facing app improvements.

prompt_templates.title: Match Existing Release Tone
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate request for consistency with previous releases.
prompt_templates.prompt: Read recent Fastlane changelog entries, identify their style, and rewrite the latest changelog so it matches their tone and length.

prompt_templates.title: Audit and Refine a Release Note
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced request for final release review.
prompt_templates.prompt: Review the proposed changelog against git history, version metadata, and recent changelog style. Fix missing user-facing changes and remove technical noise.

output_examples.input: Recent commits add gesture typing fixes, update CI workflows, and refresh translations.
output_examples.output: Welcome to Janus 2.4.1. This update improves gesture typing reliability and refreshes language translations.

output_examples.input: Recent commits include a crash fix, new keyboard theme, Gradle updates, and README edits.
output: Fixed a crash when switching keyboards.

output_examples.input: Recent commits only change release automation and internal project documentation.
output_examples.output: No user-facing app changes were found. Keep the changelog unchanged or ask for release-manager guidance.

best_practices: Review the selected base tag before drafting the changelog.
Prefer clear user benefits over technical implementation details.
Compare the draft with recent changelog files before writing it.
anti_patterns: Do not include CI, build, or repository maintenance changes unless users are affected.
Do not list every commit when a short release note is expected.
Do not invent feature names or version numbers that are not present in the project.

faq.question: What repository history does this skill review?
faq.answer: It reviews commits from the latest tag matching v* through the current HEAD.

faq.question: Which changelog file does it update?
faq.answer: It updates the highest numbered file in the documented Fastlane Android changelog directory.

faq.question: Does it include internal maintenance changes?
faq.answer: No. It is designed to exclude infrastructure, CI, build tooling, and internal documentation changes.

faq.question: Can it handle multiple important app changes?
faq.answer: Yes. It selects two to five significant user-facing changes when multiple changes matter.

faq.question: Does it verify the app version?
faq.answer: It instructs the agent to check project version metadata, such as the Gradle build file.

faq.question: Is human review still recommended?
faq.answer: Yes. A release owner should confirm the final changelog before publishing a store release.
